shots.description: Moonlit open ocean at night, already mid-Withdrawal: the whole water surface slides backward in one continuous silver sheet, exposing black glass sand at the bottom of frame. The moon-path stretches like pulled taffy, thins, and snaps. Indigo sky, ink horizon; the only brightness is the retreating silver. The slow pull-back makes the frame itself feel like it is abandoning the world.

Harbor wide by the fifteen-second mark: fishing ships keel over one by one into gleaming wet sand, masts tilting into steep silhouettes against indigo. Rigging droops; the water's edge is a bright line already far behind them. Moonlight rims every wet surface salt-white.

Close-up insert: an anchor chain, taut for one heartbeat, then slack — its links dropping into wet sand, a chain left pointing at nothing. Moonlight beads on wet iron; in soft focus behind, the silver sheet of the sea keeps walking away. Held, no drama in the cutting, all the drama in the slackening.

FRAME ONE (to be reprised wider and heavier in scene 8): high wide from the cliff's edge — the sea's retreating edge is a single bright line abandoning the land, dragging the moon's reflection toward the ink horizon. Foreground cliff grass utterly still. Composition: the bright line low in frame, enormous darkness above it.
Black. Card 1 burns in slowly, salt-white lettering on ink, as if etched by drying brine. The vast receding hiss persists faintly under the black, then drops away with the score.

subs.speaker: NARRATION
subs.text: A hundred years ago, in one night, the sea left.

shots.description: A century pours through crossfading macro details: salt crystals climb a dead hull like frost in fast-motion; kelp forests stiffen and petrify into verdigris stone; whale bones breach the whitening flats like the ribs of the world. Palette drifts from moonlit indigo toward bleached salt-white as the decades pass.

Locked-off wide of the cliff dissolving through decades: the harbor town retreats up the rock one rooftop at a time — lower houses hollow and go dark, new roofs appear higher on the cliff face. The dry seabed below whitens to bone; time-lapse cloud shadows sweep the flats. The tilt-up follows the town's climb.

FRAME TWO (to be reprised): night, the legend's present tense — a lone lamp burning at the cliff edge, one warm ember in an indigo world. Below it the darkness reads a shade too deep, deep like depth, and it visibly LEANS toward the light: the black edge bows upslope by a single wrong degree. Slow push-in until the lamp is small and surrounded.
Black. Card 2 burns in, same salt-white etching. Under the black, one distant lamp mechanism keeps ticking — the law audible before it is explained.

subs.speaker: NARRATION
subs.text: The law says every light burns till dawn.

shots.description: FRAME THREE (to be reprised): present-day Saltwick Light. The beam sweeps slow across a sea of air — a solid volumetric blade over the dry flats. Everywhere the beam is not, the black underneath reads as black that still moves like the sea being water: a faint swell, a grain of current in the dark. Card 3 burns in over the deepest black in the lower third, timed to the beam passing away from camera.
Hold on black. The wind thins away; one low call from far beneath the cliff, then nothing — a held breath before the beam whites out into the title card of scene 2.
